findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify how the fix is bounded when failing_files() yields an empty scope (e.g. treat empty scope as 'apply nothing and fall back to agent repair', or bound to files under the check's working_dir), and add a test asserting the empty-scope behaviour so AC 5's 'exactly one file' guarantee holds.
evidence: Problem statement: the old fixer 'is unscoped, so it rewrites the whole tree'
in_repair_scope docstring/code: 'if not scope: return True' — an empty scope matches everything
failing_files extracts paths only from summary text; a prettier warn line such as '[warn] Code style issues found in the above file(s). Run Prettier with --write to fix.' names no path
Testing section lists a _confined (path-traversal) rejection test but no empty-scope case; AC 5 asserts 'exactly the one file prettier flagged'
findings.finding: The scoping mechanism silently degrades to unbounded when the failure summary names no parseable file path: failing_files() returns an empty tuple and in_repair_scope() then returns True for every changed file, so every file the fix command touched is copied back — reintroducing the 'unscoped, rewrites the whole tree' defect the plan sets out to eliminate.
findings.location: Scope + Testing sections; AC line 5 ('exactly the one file prettier flagged')
scenarios: A lint/format check whose failure summary reports issues without naming an individual file path (empty scope) triggers the fix to copy back every file it modified
The named massgov-pfml acceptance run, if prettier's captured summary lacks the specific file path
findings.suggested_fix: Define the empty-scope contract in the plan: when the failure summary names no path, do not treat every changed file as in-scope; instead fall back to agent repair (or restrict to the check working_dir), and cover it with a unit test alongside the _confined test.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add an observability requirement (log or metric) that records the fix path taken — fix_command run vs. absent vs. exited non-zero vs. pod failure vs. _confined rejection — so degrade-to-agent-repair transitions are surfaced, not swallowed.
evidence: The motivating incident was invisible: 'the repair loop instead modified 16 unrelated Python files across five attempts with llm_calls=0 on every attempt, so no agent ever saw the failure.'

Testing lists silent fallbacks: 'A fix command that exits non-zero, or a pod that fails outright, degrades to agent repair rather than killing the workflow' — but no observability requirement accompanies these transitions.
No checklist/AC item requires emitting a log/metric distinguishing 'ran fix_command', 'no fix_command declared', 'fix failed -> agent repair', or 'path rejected by _confined'.
findings.finding: The plan adds a new in-pod fix execution path with multiple silent degrade-to-agent-repair transitions (no fix_command, non-zero exit, pod failure, out-of-scope path rejected) but does not specify any metric/log/trace to record which path was taken or why a fix was skipped.
scenarios: A future project's fix_command silently fails in-pod and the loop degrades to agent repair; an operator cannot tell whether the fix ran, was skipped, or errored.
findings.suggested_fix: State that _project_autofix emits a structured log/metric on each outcome (ran, skipped-no-command, non-zero-exit, pod-failure, path-rejected), and add an AC asserting the fix-skip/degrade reason is recorded.

evidence: 2 criterion line(s) bundle multiple deliverables with 'and' (split so each is independently verifiable).
verify command `grep -rn "ruff check --fix" services/` inspects output with `grep` but asserts nothing — add an exit-code or comparison (-q, [ "$(...)" -eq N ], jq -e) so a failure is observable

AC item 'A live run against `archive-massgov-pfml` reports `applied: true` with exactly t' cites operational evidence (live_run) that lives outside the codebase; tag it [non-codebase] — prefix the checkbox text with [non-codebase] so the completion verifier accepts a recorded attestation instead of failing to find code proof.
findings.suggested_fix: Split compound criteria, replace subjective terms with observable outcomes, and state how each is verified.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Define the fix command's output contract (what parse_fix_output reads) and the source of the 'repair scope' that _confined enforces (e.g. the PR's changed-file set).
evidence: 'runner.py gains run_fix, parse_fix_output, and the fix script builder'
'ci_repair.py gains failing_files and in_repair_scope'
'A fix that touches a path outside the repair scope has that path rejected by _confined' — but repair scope's source is never stated
ABSENCE: no statement of what parse_fix_output parses or what defines the confinement boundary
findings.finding: The plan names parse_fix_output, failing_files, and in_repair_scope but never defines the fix command's output contract or how the 'repair scope' that _confined enforces is derived.
findings.location: Scope / Approach — runner.py parse_fix_output, ci_repair.py failing_files/in_repair_scope, repair.py _confined
scenarios: Executor must invent the output format the fix script emits and the definition of repair scope

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State the default for gate_engine_privileged and the behavior when it is unset/false (does copy_out degrade to agent repair?).
evidence: 'scripts/config.py gains gate_engine_privileged.'
'Buildah requires privileged: true under k3s on Colima.'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add acceptance criteria (with proving unit tests) for _confined rejecting out-of-scope paths and copy-out tolerating a fix-removed file.
evidence: Testing: 'A fix that touches a path outside the repair scope has that path rejected by _confined.'
Testing: 'A tar that reports a file removed by the fix command does not fail the copy-out.'
ABSENCE: no AC line covers _confined or the tar-removed-file case
findings.finding: Two described edge-case deliverables — _confined path rejection and tar-reports-removed-file tolerance — have Testing coverage but no covering acceptance criterion.
scenarios: A regression in _confined or copy-out tar handling would not fail any acceptance criterion

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Capture the privileged-pod + copy_out architectural decision (and its security trade-off) in an ADR or AGENTS.md, not only the checks.yaml.example key.
evidence: 'pod_runner.py gains a privileged flag and copy_out, because buildah cannot unpack a layer unprivileged under k3s.'
only checks.yaml.example is listed for docs; no ADR/design-doc for the privileged-pod + copy-out decision
findings.finding: Running project-declared commands inside a privileged pod with copy-back of arbitrary changed files is a novel architectural/security decision not captured in any ADR/AGENTS.md/design doc.
findings.location: Scope — pod_runner.py privileged flag + copy_out; config/local/checks.yaml.example
scenarios: Future maintainer needs to understand why privileged pods run untrusted client fix_commands and copy files back

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add services/orchestration/gates/scanner_pod.py (PodCommandRunner / pod_command_runner) to the Scope as a consumer that threads the new `privileged` argument from settings.gate_engine_privileged into build_pod_manifest, or state explicitly why the scanner pod path is out of scope for the privileged change.
evidence: scanner_pod.py:166 `privileged=settings.gate_engine_privileged,` inside pod_command_runner()
scanner_pod.py:141 `manifest = build_pod_manifest(pod, self._namespace, self._builder_image, self._privileged)`
scanner_pod.py:128,136 PodCommandRunner __init__ gains `privileged: bool = False` / `self._privileged = privileged`

build_pod_manifest's `privileged` parameter defaults to False (pod_runner.py:62), so a scanner_pod caller left unthreaded compiles but silently retains the unprivileged behavior the plan says buildah fails under on k3s/Colima
scanner_pod.py is NOT named anywhere in the plan's Scope or Grounded assumptions
findings.finding: The plan's Scope enumerates builtin.py, checks.py, and draft_pull_request.py as the files that thread the new arguments for the build_pod_manifest `privileged` flag and the `gate_engine_privileged` setting, but services/orchestration/gates/scanner_pod.py (PodCommandRunner / pod_command_runner) is an equally affected consumer that reads settings.gate_engine_privileged and passes privileged into build_pod_manifest, and it is not enumerated.
findings.location: Scope: 'services/orchestration/gates/builtin.py, services/orchestration/temporal_activities/checks.py, and services/orchestration/temporal_workflows/draft_pull_request.py thread the new arguments.' and 'scripts/config.py gains gate_engine_privileged.'
scenarios: Semgrep/Trivy scans run through PodCommandRunner on the same k3s/Colima cluster where buildah needs privileged:true to unpack layers
An implementer follows the Scope list literally and updates only the three named files, leaving scanner_pod's pod at the old unprivileged security context
findings.suggested_fix: In Scope, extend the threading bullet to read '...builtin.py, scanner_pod.py, temporal_activities/checks.py, and draft_pull_request.py thread the new arguments,' since scanner_pod.py's PodCommandRunner also consumes gate_engine_privileged and passes it to build_pod_manifest.
